{{Short description|Theorem on linear operators}}

{{Technical|date=September 2023}}
The '''Motzkin–Taussky theorem''' is a result from [[Operator theory|operator]] and [[matrix theory]] about the representation of a sum of two bounded, [[linear operators]] (resp. matrices). The theorem was proven by [[Theodore Motzkin]] and [[Olga Taussky-Todd]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Motzkin |first1=T. S. |last2=Taussky |first2=Olga |date=1952 |title=Pairs of Matrices with Property L |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |volume=73 |issue=1 |pages=108–114 |doi=10.2307/1990825 |jstor=1990825 |pmid=16589359 |pmc=1063886 }}</ref>

The theorem is used in [[perturbation theory]], where e.g.  operators of the form 

: <math>T+xT_1</math>

are examined.

== Statement ==
Let <math>X</math> be a finite-dimensional complex [[vector space]]. Furthermore, let <math>A,B\in B(X)</math> be such that all [[Linear combination|linear combinations]] 

: <math>T=\alpha A+\beta B</math>

are [[Diagonalizable matrix|diagonalizable]] for all <math>\alpha,\beta\in \C</math>. Then all [[Eigenvalues and eigenvectors|eigenvalues]] of <math>T</math> are of the form

: <math>\lambda_{T}=\alpha\lambda_{A} + \beta \lambda_{B}</math>

(i.e. they are linear in <math>\alpha</math> und <math>\beta</math>) and <math>\lambda_{A},\lambda_{B}</math> are independent of the choice of <math>\alpha,\beta</math>.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kato |first=Tosio |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-66282-9 |title=Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators |series=Classics in Mathematics |publisher=Springer |year=1995 |volume=132 |isbn=978-3-540-58661-6 |edition=2 |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |page=86 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-66282-9}}</ref>

Here <math>\lambda_{A}</math> stands for an eigenvalue of <math>A</math>.

=== Comments ===
* Motzkin and Taussky call the above property of the linearity of the eigenvalues in <math>\alpha,\beta</math> ''property L''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Motzkin |first1=T. S. |last2=Taussky |first2=Olga |date=1955 |title=Pairs of Matrices With Property L. II |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1992996 |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |volume=80 |issue=2 |pages=387–401 |doi=10.2307/1992996 |jstor=1992996 |issn=0002-9947|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
